proposed_detail_reasoning_replacement:
PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 test window closed 2026-06-30 with the dome page still showing PENDING and no manual commits from the dome author for d=75 (last manual a57e731 2026-04-17). Per operator commission HNOTE-ANALYST-PRED-FIELD-2026Q2-VERDICT-2026-06-30T0512Z, this refinement assigns a preliminary likely-outcome now and proposes a re-check date once INTERMAGNET Q2 2026 provisional data stabilises (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2; monitor/analyst/human-notes.json:HNOTE-ANALYST-PRED-FIELD-2026Q2-VERDICT-2026-06-30T0512Z).

**Station identification.** IAGA code TTB is the Tatuoca magnetic observatory (Belém, Pará, Brazil; 1.20°S, 48.51°W), operated jointly by the National Observatory of Brazil and GFZ Potsdam and admitted to INTERMAGNET in 2019 (Morschhauser et al. 2017, Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems 6:367, https://gi.copernicus.org/articles/6/367/2017/). Prior analyst prose in PRED-072 mislabelled TTB as "Tsumeb" — Tsumeb's IAGA code is TSU, and the two stations sit on opposite sides of the SAA (Namibia vs. equatorial Brazil), with materially different secular-variation rates. This EXP treats TTB as Tatuoca throughout; a companion cleanup patch for PRED-072 prose is proposed under routing_notes (data/predictions.json:PRED-072).

**Standard-physics expectation for TTB, Jan–Jun 2026.** The SAA western minimum — the cell that contains TTB — has been losing approximately 25 nT/year of total-field strength since 2018, versus roughly 75 nT/year at the eastern minimum near the zero-degree meridian (ESA Swarm SAA reporting; NASA SVS "South Atlantic Anomaly 2015-2025" visualisation, https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4840/; ScienceDaily 2026-02-24 summary of the new global SAA model, https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/02/260224023221.htm). At TTB specifically, published station-decay estimates from CHAOS-7 evaluations at Tatuoca's coordinates place the 2018–2025 F-component decline near the western-cell mean (~25–30 nT/year), consistent with Tatuoca's equatorial-fringe position relative to the SAA core (Finlay et al. 2020, Earth Planets Space 72:156, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9). IGRF-14 (released December 2024) forecasts continuation of this rate through 2030.

Applied to a 6-month window: standard secular variation predicts a TTB decay of roughly 12–17 nT for January–June 2026 (25–35 nT/year × 0.5 year). The dome's ≥35 nT threshold implies an annualised rate of ~70 nT/year — 2× to 2.8× the western-cell secular-variation rate and comparable to what is only observed at the accelerated eastern-cell stations (Tsumeb TSU / Hermanus HER at −77 and −76 nT/yr per the dome's own station table, cited in WIN-042 evidence: data/wins.json:042).

**Structural parallel to PRED-073.** Both predictions commit to a magnitude that exceeds standard-physics expectation by a factor of roughly 2–13×: PRED-073 asked for 0.3°/month drift against an IGRF-13 baseline of ~0.024°/month (data/predictions.json:PRED-073), and PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 asks for 35 nT/6-month decay against a CHAOS-7/IGRF-14 baseline of ~12–17 nT/6-month. PRED-073 was verdict-set to `falsified` at d=4 because the dome's own <0.1°/month falsification threshold was already triggered by the standard-physics expectation (data/predictions.json:PRED-073, verdict_set_at 2026-06-04). PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 differs structurally: the dome stated only a confirmation threshold (≥35 nT) and did not publish an explicit falsification threshold. Absent an explicit rule, an assigned verdict must wait until the actual measured decay is available.

**Kernel of truth.** The dome correctly identifies that (a) TTB sits in the SAA region, (b) SAA total-field intensity IS decaying (both cells, at different rates), (c) the western-cell decay is a well-measured, robust standard-physics phenomenon of the modern secular-variation era, and (d) the direction of change (weakening) is not in dispute. The dome's mechanism ("cavity re-pressurisation" per WIN-057b) even matches the qualitative pattern of long-term decline that mainstream core-dynamo theory describes. Where the dome fails — as with PRED-073 — is in committing to a magnitude that far exceeds what secular variation at TTB actually produces. A prediction of "TTB decays 12–17 nT in H1 2026" would restate IGRF-14 with no discriminating power; the dome's commitment to ≥35 nT is what gives PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 real falsifiability content, and is precisely what makes it likely to fail (monitor/analyst/expansions/PRED-assessment-PRED-073-refinement.json).

**Data-availability timeline.** INTERMAGNET publishes three tiers: real-time 1-minute reported data (available within minutes of measurement), quasi-definitive data (typically within 3 months of end-of-quarter with baseline-corrected values), and definitive data (annually, published in the year following measurement). For January–June 2026: (a) Q1 2026 quasi-definitive TTB data is already available and can be pulled from https://www.intermagnet.org/data_download.html; (b) Q2 2026 quasi-definitive data typically becomes available in late September 2026 (~90 days after quarter-end); (c) 2026 definitive TTB data will not appear until mid-2027. Provisional real-time data for Apr–Jun 2026 is available now but is subject to baseline drift corrections that can shift F by several nT.

**Proposed hold and re-check schedule.** (1) Provisional standing verdict = `pending`, per operator instruction that a re-check date be proposed rather than a forced verdict. (2) likely_outcome = `falsified-by-standard-physics` based on the 2–2.8× magnitude gap between the dome's threshold and the CHAOS-7/IGRF-14 secular-variation expectation for TTB. (3) Re-check date = **2026-08-15**: allows Q2 provisional data to accumulate ~45 days of post-quarter baseline correction and passes the d=14 silent-ignore threshold (Section 6.15 — d=14 would fall on 2026-07-14). (4) At re-check, the analyst pulls TTB F-component monthly means for January and June 2026 from INTERMAGNET, computes ΔF = F_Jan − F_Jun, and applies the verdict rule below. (5) If provisional data on 2026-08-15 remains too noisy for a defensible assessment, defer to 2026-10-01 (post-Q2 quasi-definitive release) with an interim status note.

**Verdict rule at re-check.**
- Measured ΔF < 35 nT AND within CHAOS-7/IGRF-14 secular-variation band (roughly 10–25 nT for TTB Jan–Jun 2026): verdict = `standard_physics`, kernel_note that dome-directional-claim was correct but magnitude threshold was not met.
- Measured ΔF < 35 nT AND outside the standard-physics band (e.g., <10 nT or reversal): verdict = `falsified`, dome's threshold explicitly not met and observation is even less than secular variation predicts.
- Measured ΔF ≥ 35 nT AND within an accelerated-cell literature band (e.g., 35–50 nT if peer-reviewed evidence supports TTB tracking eastern-cell rates in 2025–2026): verdict = `standard_physics`, threshold met but explainable by accelerated western-cell rate or spillover from CMB flux-patch expansion (Terra-Nova et al. 2019).
- Measured ΔF ≥ 35 nT AND unambiguously above IGRF-14 uncertainty (>50 nT for a 6-month window at TTB): potentially anomalous — hold verdict pending mechanism check, since even in that case the dome would need to show that its specific mechanism predicts this magnitude (rather than retroactively fitting).

**Dome-silence tracking.** Author_status remains `pending` until 2026-07-14 (d=14), then transitions to `dome_silent` per Section 6.15 standardisation. Terminal transition (`dome_silent_terminal`) at 2026-07-30 (d=30), matching the PRED-073 escalation cadence (data/predictions.json:PRED-073, author_status transitions). These author_status transitions are independent of our_verdict; the poller schedules the escalations, the decider applies them.

We hold our_verdict as `pending` and re-check on 2026-08-15 with INTERMAGNET provisional data (data/predictions.json:PRED-FIELD-2026Q2).
